t: Section 3082 of title 7, Canal Zone Code, is amended by inserting after “bond”, and preceding “the failure.”, the words “for any injury to the estate or a person interested therein, arising from”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment inserting words into a Canal Zone Code provision about liability on a bond for injury to an estate. The only tempting hook is the phrase "a person interested therein", but that describes who may be injured under a bond, not any outside party consulting on, commenting on, or challenging a federal decision. There is no rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or grant of a right to sue the government.

opus.w: This amendment only changes the wording of a Canal Zone Code provision so that a bond covers injury to an estate or to people interested in it. It does not set up any comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to challenge a federal decision. The mention of persons interested in an estate concerns private liability on a fiduciary's bond, not outsiders taking part in federal decisions.
opus.s: the words “for any injury to the estate or a person interested therein, arising from”
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The words "a person interested therein" and liability for "injury" could look like they give an outside party a right to sue. That reading fails. This is a technical amendment to the Canal Zone Code about who an estate representative's bond covers. It concerns private liability on a probate bond. It doesn't involve a federal decision or give anyone a right to challenge one.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a textual amendment to a code section regarding liability for injuries. It defines who can claim injury (a person interested in the estate) but does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in a federal decision-making process. The mention of 'a person' is part of a legal definition of standing or liability, not a procedural requirement for public input.
qwen_chat.s: Section 3082 of title 7, Canal Zone Code, is amended by inserting after “bond”, and preceding “the failure.”, the words “for any injury to the estate or a person interested therein, arising from”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "a person interested therein" refers to an outside party participating in a legal process. However, this is merely a textual amendment defining the scope of liability for injuries to an estate. It does not establish a process for consultation, comment, or advisory input from outside parties into a federal decision-making process. It is a substantive legal definition, not a procedural participation mechanism.
